title: Palo Alto Networks Firewall Overview
description: Palo Alto Networks next-generation firewalls enforce network security policy (traffic, threat, and URL inspection, IPsec VPN, routing) and are managed centrally through Panorama. This dashboard covers firewall reachability, management-plane and dataplane resources, hardware environment, IPsec tunnels, BGP and OSPF routing, licenses, interfaces, HA links, and firewall logs.

definition.content:
Palo Alto Networks next-generation firewalls enforce network security policy (traffic, threat, and URL inspection, IPsec VPN, routing) and are managed centrally through Panorama. This dashboard covers firewall reachability, management-plane and dataplane resources, hardware environment, IPsec tunnels, BGP and OSPF routing, licenses, interfaces, HA links, and firewall logs.

- [Datadog integration documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/pan_firewall/)
- [Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS documentation](https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/pan-os)
Key health and activity signals at a glance for quick detection of problems and drill-down into the relevant section.

definition.description: Number of firewalls the integration reported on in the selected time range, reachable or not.
definition.title: Firewalls

definition.description: Firewalls whose API did not respond to the latest check run in the selected time range. 0 means every firewall currently answers.
definition.title: Unreachable firewalls

definition.description: IPsec tunnels that were active for the whole selected time range: both their lowest and highest state readings are active. Tunnels that were inactive or initializing at any point are not counted.
definition.title: Tunnels up the whole range

definition.description: IPsec tunnels that are currently inactive, from their latest state reading in the selected time range. See the IPsec VPN section for which ones.
definition.title: Inactive IPsec tunnels

definition.description: Panorama hosts whose latest discovery call in the selected time range failed. Collection continues: the integration keeps polling the firewalls from the last list Panorama returned, but firewalls added to Panorama during the outage are not discovered. Only applies when firewalls are discovered through Panorama; shows No data otherwise. Ignores the firewall filter, since Panorama is not tied to one firewall.
definition.title: Panorama unreachable

definition.description: BGP peers that are currently not established, from their latest status reading in the selected time range. See the BGP peers table for which ones.
definition.title: BGP peers down

definition.description: Reachable firewalls by current high-availability state. The HA state is a tag, so after a failover a firewall reports under a new series; this widget uses a fixed 15-minute window so each firewall appears in one slice only. Hover a slice to see which firewalls it contains. Standalone firewalls without HA are not shown.
definition.title: HA state of reachable firewalls

definition.description: The three licenses closest to expiry on the selected firewalls, per firewall and feature, from the latest license reading. License data is reported every 24 hours, so this widget uses a fixed 2-day window instead of the dashboard time range. Perpetual licenses are not included.
definition.title: Soonest-expiring licenses

definition.description: Status of the Datadog monitors tagged `integration:pan-firewall`.
definition.title: Monitors

definition.content: Management-plane CPU and memory per firewall, plus the busiest dataplane core, fullest file system, hottest sensor, and sensors in temperature or power alarm across the selected firewalls.

definition.description: Management-plane CPU used per firewall. The management plane runs the web UI, API, logging, and commits; high values slow management tasks but not traffic forwarding.
definition.title: Management CPU used

definition.description: Management-plane memory in use (not available to processes) and swap used, as a percentage of total, per firewall. Sustained swap use means the management plane is short of memory.
definition.title: Management memory and swap used

definition.description: Highest data-plane core utilization across the selected firewalls in the time range. The data plane forwards traffic, so a saturated core can drop or delay packets.
definition.title: Max dataplane CPU

definition.description: Fullest file system across the selected firewalls in the time range, excluding the log partition `/opt/panlogs`, which PAN-OS fills up to the log quota and purges by design. Reported every 30 minutes. A full config or root partition can block commits and content updates.
definition.title: Max disk used

definition.description: Hottest temperature sensor reading across the selected firewalls in the time range. Virtual firewalls (VM-Series) have no sensors and show No data.
definition.title: Max temperature

definition.description: Temperature and power sensors that were in alarm at some point in the selected time range. Virtual firewalls (VM-Series) have no sensors and show 0.
definition.title: Sensors in alarm

definition.description: Management-plane CPU time by category, averaged across the selected firewalls. High iowait points at disk contention; steal (VM-Series only) means the hypervisor is short of CPU.
definition.title: Management CPU breakdown

definition.content: Per-tunnel state and traffic. State: green is active, yellow is initializing, red is inactive. Down in window flags a tunnel that was inactive at any point in the time range. An active tunnel with no received traffic usually points at the peer.

definition.description: **State** is the tunnel's current state: `1` active (green), `2` initializing (yellow), `0` inactive (red). **Down in window** is `1` (red) if the tunnel was inactive at any point in the selected time range, otherwise `0`. **Received** and **Sent** are average byte rates over the time range; they are empty for tunnels that share a tunnel interface.
definition.title: Tunnel state

definition.description: Received byte rate for the ten busiest IPsec tunnels.
definition.title: Tunnel traffic received (top 10)

definition.description: Sent byte rate for the ten busiest IPsec tunnels.
definition.title: Tunnel traffic sent (top 10)

definition.content: BGP peer state and route exchange, and OSPF adjacencies. Down peers are listed first. OSPF widgets need `collect_ospf: true`.

definition.description: BGP peers that restarted (their session came up less than 30 minutes earlier) at some point in the selected time range. Repeated restarts mean a flapping peer.
definition.title: BGP peers restarted

definition.description: BGP connections dropped in the selected time range. Reported only by the Advanced Routing Engine; shows No data for firewalls on the legacy routing engine.
definition.title: BGP connections dropped

definition.description: OSPF neighbors whose adjacency is not in the Full state. Requires `collect_ospf: true` in the integration configuration; shows No data while OSPF collection is off (the default). On a shared segment with three or more routers, two neighbors that are both DROther stay in 2-Way by design and are counted here.
definition.title: OSPF neighbors not full

definition.description: OSPF neighbor adjacency state changes in the selected time range. Sent only by the Advanced Routing Engine, and requires `collect_ospf: true` in the integration configuration; shows No data while OSPF collection is off (the default).
definition.title: OSPF neighbor state changes

definition.description: One row per BGP peer, down peers first. **Status**: 1 (green) established, 0 (red) not established. **Time in status**: how long the peer has been in its current status; the legacy routing engine reports 0 for a peer that never came up. **Restarted (last 30 min)**: 1 (yellow) if the session came up in the last 30 minutes at any point in the time range; repeated 1s mean the peer is flapping.
definition.title: BGP peers

definition.description: Prefixes accepted from each established peer, summed across address families. A sudden drop means the peer withdrew routes.
definition.title: Accepted prefixes by peer

definition.description: Accepted prefixes as a percentage of each peer's configured limit, highest address family per peer. Above 80% the peer is close to being torn down for exceeding its limit.
definition.title: Prefix limit used

definition.content: Interfaces with the most errors and drops, dataplane drops by aspect, HA link errors, and interfaces receiving spoofing and malformed-packet attacks.

definition.description: Interfaces with the most receive errors, receive drops, forwarding errors, and flow-state drops in the selected time range, combined.
definition.title: Interfaces with most errors and drops

definition.description: Data-plane packet drops by cause (aspect), such as session, resource, or tunnel. A growing resource or session aspect means the firewall is running out of capacity. Requires `collect_global_counters: true` in the integration configuration; shows No data while global counter collection is off (the default).
definition.title: Dropped packets by aspect

definition.description: Receive errors and drops on the HA1 and HA2 links per firewall. Errors on these links can delay HA state sync or cause a false failover.
definition.title: HA link errors and drops

definition.description: Packets dropped by zone protection as IP spoofing, MAC spoofing, LAND, ping-of-death, or teardrop attacks. Empty is normal. Requires zone protection profiles on the zones; without them these counters stay at 0 even under attack.
definition.title: Attack packets by type

definition.description: Received byte rate for the ten busiest interfaces across the selected firewalls.
definition.title: Interface traffic received (top 10)

definition.description: Sent byte rate for the ten busiest interfaces across the selected firewalls.
definition.title: Interface traffic sent (top 10)

definition.description: Security rules with the most hits in the selected time range, summed across the selected firewalls. Use the firewall filter to see one firewall.
definition.title: Top security rules by hits

definition.description: Security rules sorted by hits, fewest first, summed across the selected firewalls. Rules with 0 hits (yellow) over a long time range, such as 7 or 30 days, may be unused or shadowed by a rule above them. Rules excluded by the integration's rule filter are not listed.
definition.title: Least-used security rules

definition.content: Expired licenses, days until each licensed feature expires, and whether the check can authenticate to the firewall API. Panorama reachability is in the Overview.

definition.description: Licenses that are currently expired, from the latest license reading in the last 2 days. License data is reported every 24 hours, so this widget uses a fixed 2-day window instead of the dashboard time range. An expired threat or URL filtering license stops content updates for that feature.
definition.title: Expired licenses

definition.description: Firewalls that rejected the integration's API credentials in the selected time range. Check the API key or user configured for the integration.
definition.title: API authentication failures

definition.description: Days until each license expires, per firewall and feature, lowest first, from the latest license reading. License data is reported every 24 hours, so this widget uses a fixed 2-day window instead of the dashboard time range. Perpetual licenses are not listed.
definition.title: License days left

definition.content: Threat log events by severity, threat type, and flagged client IP. Threat counts come from logs, not metrics.

definition.description: Threat log events by severity. Requires Palo Alto Networks Firewall log collection; shows No data without it. Follows the firewall filter through the logs' device_hostname attribute; the Panorama filter does not apply to logs.
definition.title: Threats by severity

definition.description: Most frequent threat log subtypes, such as virus, spyware, or vulnerability. Requires Palo Alto Networks Firewall log collection. Follows the firewall filter through the logs' device_hostname attribute; the Panorama filter does not apply to logs.
definition.title: Top threat types

definition.description: Client IPs that triggered the most threat log events. Requires Palo Alto Networks Firewall log collection. Follows the firewall filter through the logs' device_hostname attribute; the Panorama filter does not apply to logs.
definition.title: Top flagged client IPs

definition.content: Firewall logs forwarded from PAN-OS: critical-severity entries and log volume by status. For traffic, threat, and authentication log views, open the Palo Alto Networks Firewall Logs dashboard.

definition.description: Recent Palo Alto Networks Firewall logs with critical status, which the log pipeline sets from PAN-OS critical severity; high and medium severity map to warning and are not listed. The device_name column is the firewall that sent the log. Follows the firewall filter through the logs' device_hostname attribute.
definition.title: Critical logs

definition.description: Palo Alto Networks Firewall log volume over time by status. A drop to zero means logs stopped arriving. Follows the firewall filter through the logs' device_hostname attribute; the Panorama filter does not apply to logs.
definition.title: Logs by status
